summary: Material change since the prior snapshot: Saudi Arabia officially confirmed that several drones launched from Iraq targeted the East-West Pipeline, after the Ministry of Energy had already shut the line as a precaution following multiple attacks. Saudi Arabia is not retaliating at this stage at Iraq's request, but reserves the right to protect its infrastructure. This raises confidence that the main Saudi oil route bypassing Hormuz is itself exposed to cross-border attack risk. No new U.S., Taiwan or China official macro release was identified since the prior snapshot; September 11 market closes remain the latest verified values.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: The combination of near-5% U.S. long yields and persistent Middle East energy/logistics disruption remains a valuation and margin headwind for Taiwan equities, especially long-duration technology and energy-intensive sectors. Strong AI/HPC export demand remains an offset.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Semantic interpretation is downstream research input only.

key_drivers.name: Saudi East-West Pipeline attack attribution becomes official
key_drivers.observed: Saudi Arabia officially said several drones launched from Iraq targeted the East-West Pipeline. The line had already been shut as a precaution after multiple attacks; injuries and damage were reported.
key_drivers.interpretation: The principal Saudi bypass around Hormuz is itself exposed to cross-border attack risk, increasing persistence risk for global energy logistics.

key_drivers.name: U.S. August CPI remains a hawkish-rate input
key_drivers.observed: Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y; core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y.
key_drivers.interpretation: Near-term Fed tightening risk remains elevated and long-duration equity discount rates remain restrictive.

key_drivers.name: Oil/freight shock remains embedded
key_drivers.observed: Brent settled September 11 at US$104.61 and WTI at US$100.05; Gulf-to-Asia tanker freight had already reached record levels.
key_drivers.interpretation: Taiwan remains exposed through imported energy, freight, insurance, FX and global-rate channels.

key_risks: A sustained U.S. 10Y yield near 5% can compress long-duration semiconductor and AI hardware valuation multiples.
Simultaneous security risk around Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and the Saudi East-West Pipeline can keep delivered energy and shipping costs elevated.
Saudi Arabia's decision not to retaliate immediately reduces near-term escalation risk, but attribution to drones launched from Iraq increases regional spillover risk.
Taiwan's strong AI/HPC export cycle offsets but does not eliminate energy, FX and global-rate risks.
Copper and the September 11 USD/TWD close remain stale in this semantic snapshot because no sufficiently authoritative new value was inserted.

policy_tone.global: Energy-security risk remains inflationary while also raising downside risk to global real demand.
